messages:
ci-bot: [ALERT] pipeline: main — integration/gpu-e2e failed after merge (job 4821). https://ci.redwood.example/runs/4821 :rotating_light:

maria: @jonathan your PR (#4521) went in ~6m ago, looks like it brought this red. Can you take a look?

jonathan: on it. I'm running a quick bisect locally to see if it's my change or a flake.

jonathan: quick log snippet from the failing run:
```
AssertionError: expected 0.98 to be within tolerance of 1.0
  at tests/e2e/gpu/inference_accuracy_test.py:87
  GPU node: gpu-7
```

sophie: iirc we rolled out a new nvidia driver image yesterday to some pools, CC @infra-oncall — could be coincidental.

kevin: if it's only on GPU nodes that points to infra. But the assertion looks model-output-y too, might be nondeterministic.

maria: can someone trigger a rerun of just that job? dont want to rerun full pipeline.

infra-oncall: rerun kicked off: `ci rerun job 4821 --target=integration/gpu-e2e` — job 4821.2 started.

ci-bot: rerun finished: job 4821.2 failed again (same test).

jonathan: thanks. I'm going to bisect between main@~10m and the commit from my PR. If anyone sees obvious env diffs (drivers, docker base), call it out.

kevin: quick check — the `gpu-runtime:2025-11-30` image moved to a new kernel patch on 2025-12-03 at 02:14 UTC. That coincides with last infra deploy.

jonathan: interesting. My PR didn't touch infra images, just changed tokenizer padding behavior. But that could alter beam search timing and numeric rounding.

sophie: could we try running the failing test with deterministic seeds and fp32 fallback? e.g. `pytest tests/e2e/gpu/inference_accuracy_test.py::test_topk_consistency -k gpu --seed=42 --env=FP32_FALLBACK=1`

jonathan: running isolated repro on gpu-7 now. If it reproduces I'll push a quick fix or a test tweak (mark flaky) until we triage.

infra-oncall: FYI we've temporarily pinned `gpu-runtime` back to `2025-11-28` on a canary pool, will monitor for new failures.

jonathan: repro reproduced locally: same assertion. With FP32_FALLBACK=1 it passes. That suggests a precision/driver interaction.

maria: given customer-facing risk, do we want a revert or a test quarantine?

jonathan: I'll open a rollback PR for the tokenizer change to be safe, and also open an issue to debug numeric nondeterminism with the infra team. Will label both `urgent` and `ci-red`.

kevin: sounds good. For now i'll add `# flaky-gpu` marker to that test in CI so main is unblocked; update must be small and documented.

jonathan: created revert PR #4530 and an issue tracking gpu nondet: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/issues/987. pinging @infra-oncall for follow-up on image roll.

maria: thanks everyone — setting a short post-merge hold until revert lands. If infra finds a driver root cause we can revert the pin. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: PR #4530 (revert) merged. main pipeline re-run triggered.

ci-bot: main pipeline now green. All good for now.

maria: excellent. Closing loop — action items: jonathan follow up on issue 987; infra team verify driver/patch impact and report back in #eng-infra.

jonathan: will do, thanks all.
